objective: Close native macOS integration hardening: Shortcuts fallback, curated App Intents, and release gates must be honest, typed, and fail closed.

criteria.promise: Shortcuts integration runs only existing user-owned shortcuts through /usr/bin/shortcuts with separated arguments, bounded stdout/stderr, real exit-code errors, mapping validation and foreground requirements.
The curated App Intents surface exposes exactly the 16 supported launcher/Brain commands, reversible deep links, and unknown IDs remain unavailable.
Release hardening checks the signed artifact for required usage descriptions, universal macOS slices, and absence of App Sandbox while the architecture relies on Full Disk Access.

verification_gates.procedure: Inspect Shortcuts.swift, ShortcutActionHandler.swift, BELShortcutMapping and run focused Shortcut tests.
verification_gates.expected: No shell interpolation, missing tool/non-zero exit/control-name failures are typed and tested.

verification_gates.procedure: Inspect AppIntents.swift and BELAppIntentCatalog; run App Intent catalog tests.
verification_gates.expected: 16 curated intents and shortcuts are verified; unknown deep links/actions fail closed.

verification_gates.procedure: Inspect Scripts/release-mac.sh and Scripts/BeLauncher.entitlements; run N7 release hardening tests.
verification_gates.expected: Release script checks usage keys, universal binary and sandbox absence; entitlements do not enable sandbox.

recon_evidence: Shortcuts, ShortcutActionHandler, AppIntents, App Intent catalog tests, release hardening tests and entitlements were inspected. This ticket verifies the already-implemented native macOS hardening without claiming MacBook runtime TCC proof.

first_checkpoint.evidence: Focused native integration test matrix and scoped diff/inspection notes.
